reported_success.quote: The results of Experiment 1a provided a direct replication of Aguado et al. (2009) in a within-subjects design and using the same faces that had been used in the original study.

notes: Full primary papers are available and titles/DOIs verified; this is test-selection ambiguity, not paper unavailability. No arbitrary choice among eligible tests was made. Original p. 13 candidate participant-level interactions: Expression Task, F(1,15) = 11.47, p < .05, partial eta-squared = .43; Sex Task, F(1,15) = 9.96, p < .05, partial eta-squared = .39. Each uses 16 participants (p. 11: 32 participants split equally between conditions). Original item-level interactions on the same page: expression task F(1,28) = 38.37, p < .001, partial eta-squared = .57; sex task F(1,28) = 8.44, p < .05, partial eta-squared = .23. Replication p. 1287 candidate interactions: expression task F(1, 23) = 19.73, p < .001, partial eta-squared = .462; sex task F(1, 23) = 8.79, p = .007, partial eta-squared = .276. Both replication tasks use the same 24 participants, with reaction times faster than 100 ms or outside three individual SDs removed. These are separately printed tests, not interchangeable values. The authors provide an Experiment 1a-level successful replication narrative; that verdict does not resolve which task the assigned effect intends. Field statistics remain null pending an unambiguous task and participant/item locator.
